trends.name: Compromised cloud service provider credentials enabling broad multi-tenant access
trends.rationale: Multiple articles document how a single compromised cloud provider credential cascades across many enterprise customers. ConnectWise Cloud Backup's compromised M365 credential enabled unauthorized access to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants (Oct 17, Oct 19-20), with ConnectWise responding by disabling cloud backups, resetting credentials, and strengthening access protections (Oct 20). Railway disclosed unauthorized third-party access to encrypted environment variables storing customer secrets (Oct 22). This pattern demonstrates systemic risk in cloud infrastructure dependencies.

trends.name: Credential-stealing malware targeting AI development tools and IDE interfaces
trends.rationale: Multiple attacks demonstrate credential harvesting from AI development tools themselves becoming attack vectors. Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop preview pane contained a zero-click vulnerability enabling silent credential theft of SSH keys, AWS credentials, and Claude OAuth tokens (Oct 14). GhostAction disguised credential stealer malware within a fake font file to target developers (Oct 19). LiteLLM's supply chain attack involved GitHub token theft from logs (Oct 21-22). This pattern shows attackers targeting developer infrastructure as a vector to compromise downstream applications.
